title: Ms. Frizzle and a Red Panda join LEGO Ideas' second 2026 review

bodyMarkdown:

Ms. Frizzle and the Magic School Bus, designed by wilderland, is based on the 1990s PBS animated series and comes in at under 700 pieces. It features a brick-built yellow bus with a removable roof, full interior, removable wings and engine, plus panels to revert it to its original school bus look. Red Panda: Bamboo Sanctuary, from designer AoKI_Sudzuki, is a display-style build of the animal alongside bamboo, plants and shoots, sitting on a natural-look base with a small sign. Most of the model is fixed in pose, though the head reportedly moves.

These additions bring the current review round closer to 100 qualifying fan designs, joining projects already confirmed for review, including Green Iguana Mecha, The Stag of Seasons, The Addams Family, Coastal Keepsake Box Display and Height Chart for Children.

Reaching 10K supporters means these projects move forward to LEGO's review stage - it does not confirm they will become official sets.

For LEGO Ideas fans, this is a good moment to check in on which niche fan concepts are progressing towards a possible official release. A growing review pool also means more variety, from nostalgic TV tie-ins to nature-themed display pieces, giving collectors and custom builders fresh inspiration even before any set is greenlit.

title: New LEGO flame piece brings back a classic fire-building trick
summary: A new flame element that first appeared as a minifigure accessory this year is letting builders recreate multi-piece fire trails, a technique lost when LEGO retired the connecting flame piece back in 2016.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A new LEGO flame element, first seen as a minifigure accessory in 76335 Spider-Man vs. Ghost Rider Motorcycle, has since turned up in several other sets including 40883 Halloween Skull Candle, 76354 S.H.I.E.L.D. Helicarrier and 76466 Philosopher's Stone – Collectors' Edition.

Brick Fanatics has been testing the piece and reckons it could be the biggest upgrade to LEGO fire building since the original flame element was introduced back in 1993. That classic piece had small bars at its base, letting builders link multiple flames together into trails — a popular technique that disappeared when LEGO retired it in 2016 in favour of a version (first released in 2008) without those connectors.

Using BrickLink Studio, Brick Fanatics experimented with the new element's connection points — a bar, a stud with a hole, and an anti-stud space — and found a way to link multiple flames again. It's not quite as neat as the original 1993 technique, but it's described as genuinely functional for building convincing flame trails.

## Why it matters
Fire and flame effects are a staple for MOC builders, diorama makers and anyone building bonfires, torches or fiery scenery into custom models and displays. A piece that finally makes multi-flame trails possible again is a small but useful win for the building-technique toolbox, especially for Bricks in a Bag customers working on custom scenes or stadium-adjacent display builds needing fire effects.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for more sets featuring this new flame element, and expect the building community to keep refining techniques for using it in bonfires, torches and other fiery MOC details.

title: LEGO Doctor Doom minifigures compared: 2013 original vs two new 2026 versions
summary: A new comparison from LEGO Fan Media creator just2good lines up the classic 2013 Doctor Doom minifigure against two brand-new versions arriving this September.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO's only Doctor Doom minifigure has been the one from 2013's 76005 Spider-Man: Daily Bugle Showdown, a set that retired in 2015 and has since become pricey on the secondary market. That's about to change, as two new sets featuring Doctor Doom minifigures – 76340 Advent Calendar and 76345 Doctor Doom Bust – are set to release on 1 September 2026.

Creator just2good got early access to all three minifigures and put them side by side. The original 2013 figure has a smaller dark green hood and cape, a lighter shade of green on the torso and legs, and a comic-inspired face print with visible skin tone behind the eyes.

The Advent Calendar version keeps a similar silhouette but switches to a fully light-green colour scheme, adds much more detailed torso and leg printing, uses the newer rubber cape instead of fabric, and drops the visible skin tone for a more sinister look.

The Doctor Doom Bust minifigure is different again, based on the Robert Downey Jr version of the character from Avengers: Doomsday.

## Why it matters
For collectors, this ends a 13-year gap where the only way to get a Doctor Doom minifigure was paying inflated resale prices, reportedly over £60. Having two affordable, current-production options at different price points gives fans genuine choice, whether they want the classic comic look or the newer movie-inspired design.

## What to watch next
Both sets are due out on 1 September 2026 – worth checking official LEGO channels closer to release for confirmed pricing and availability.

title: Two LEGO Ideas Interstellar bookend sets hit 10,000 votes days apart

This comes just days after a near-identical concept, *Interstellar: A Look Back in Time Bookend*, hit the same milestone.

Both builds recreate the film's famous bookcase/tesseract scene as a separable bookend, but with different approaches. The newer set is a bit smaller at just under 600 pieces, and adds diorama touches like the Interstellar logo and a quote piece.

Interestingly, the designer behind this latest project, Minibrick41587, already has three other projects that have hit 10,000 votes in this review round, including Remy the Little Chef, plus Hamilton and Miffy-themed builds.

**Rumour/speculation:** It's not confirmed whether either Interstellar project will become an official set. ## Why it matters
For LEGO Ideas followers and Interstellar fans, this is a fun example of how the platform can throw up overlapping concepts. It also raises genuine questions about how the LEGO Group might handle judging two similar entries in the same review - something collectors will want to watch closely if they're hoping for an official Interstellar set.
